intent: Deliver a local Chrome/Edge overlay that reads committed Wallz board state and recommends legal pawn moves and walls for manual practice, hot-seat and private friend games. Search must be bounded, keep the page responsive, and invalidate advice when state changes; joining and submitting moves remain manual.
residual_risks: The active synchronous search finishes within its selected budget before queued messages are processed. Latest advice can wait for the remainder of that budget plus its own search; this documented latency is distinct from the rejected backlog claim.
The reader depends on committed React fiber and Wallz board metadata. A site update may require a reader update; unrecognised positions currently fail closed with an error.
Deeper wall search is selective and can miss long-term setups. The small local benchmark is a sanity check, not an Elo estimate or proof of optimal play.
testing_gaps: No live smoke or deterministic fixture exercises extension/bridge.js:35,42 hot-seat classification and player/orientation changes across hot-seat turns, although README.md lists that mode as supported.
The native worker burst reproduction uses a synthetic 250ms synchronous analysis. Current-state latency during a real Deep search in a Chromium Manifest V3 worker remains unmeasured.
Edge compatibility is inferred from Chromium extension support and has not been separately tested.
